text: Surprised and uneasy. <break time="0.8s" /> Hauchecorne swallowed his drink. <break time="0.8s" /> And followed the officer. <break time="0.8s" /> To the mayors office. <break time="0.8s" /> The mayor, a large, serious man. <break time="0.8s" /> Told him that someone had seen him. <break time="0.8s" /> Pick up the lost pocketbook. <break time="0.8s" /> When Hauchecorne asked. <break time="0.8s" /> Who had said such a thing. <break time="0.8s" /> The mayor answered. <break time="0.8s" /> Monsieur Malandain, the harness maker. <break time="0.8s" /> Red with anger. <break time="0.8s" /> The old man pulled the string. <break time="0.8s" /> From his pocket. <break time="0.8s" /> And showed it to the mayor. <break time="0.8s" /> He saw me pick up this string. <break time="0.8s" /> And that is the reason why I bent down. <break time="0.8s" /> He cried. <break time="0.8s" /> The mayor shook his head. <break time="0.8s" /> And said that an honest man like Malandain. <break time="0.8s" /> Would never mistake a string for a pocketbook. <break time="0.8s" /> Hauchecorne raised his hand. <break time="0.8s" /> And swore on his honor. <break time="0.8s" /> Speaking as if God himself were listening. <break time="0.8s" /> The mayor added that he had searched the mud for a long time. <break time="0.8s" /> Looking for coins that had fallen out. <break time="0.8s" /> Malandain was brought in and repeated his story. <break time="0.8s" /> And the two men argued angrily. <break time="0.8s" /> For a whole hour. <break time="0.8s" /> They searched Hauchecorne. <break time="0.8s" /> At his own request. <break time="0.8s" /> But found nothing. <break time="0.8s" /> So the puzzled mayor. <break time="0.8s" /> Let him go for now.
